newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan firms' profits to rise 10.4% in 97/98 - Wako.
newsitem.headline: Japan firms' profits to rise 10.4% in 97/98 - Wako.

text.p: Current profits at major Japanese companies are expected to increase by an average of 10.4 percent in the current business year to March 1998, Wako Research Institute said on Thursday.
The research company, affiliated with Wako Securities Co, also predicted that the rate of growth in the companies' parent current profits will decline slightly to 9.1 percent in 1998/99.
Current profit is pre-tax and includes gains and losses from non-operating activities.
The electronics industry will lead in profit growth in both 1997/98 and 1998/99, followed by the transportation equipment and steel sectors, Wako said.
The performance of electronics manufacturers will be boosted by the stabilisation of chip prices and robust sales of computers and digital audio-visual equipment, it said.
In 1997/98, parent current profits in the manufacturing sector will slow to 10.4 percent from 19.8 percent in 1996/97, as the benefits of the weak yen fade, Wako said.
The research firm expects the dollar-yen rate to average 115 yen per dollar in both 1997/98 and 1998/99.
Profits in the non-manufacturing sector in 1997/98 are forecast to improve significantly, rising 10.3 percent from a year earlier compared with a decline of 3.9 percent in the prior fiscal year.

In 1998/99, the electronics sector's current profits are expected to maintain double-digit growth, buoyed by continuous expansion of computer production and mass production of 64 megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips.
Profits in the steel industry are forecast to rise by 61.2 percent in 1998/99 due to an increase in production and cost-cutting measures, the research firm said.
The Wako survey covered 264 major companies listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, excluding financial institutions.
